title: Curved-Crease Origami: Strengthening Huzita-Hatori (S8 — constructive HH-3 parallel case)
description: S2 ORIENT scaffold + S4 constructive HH-2 (perpendicular bisector) + S5 constructive HH-4 (perpendicular through a point) + S6 constructive HH-7 (Hatori fold, non-parallel case) for the open question: can the seven straight-crease Huzita-Hatori axioms (`AngleTrisectionOQ05.HHAxioms`) be strengthened to capture curved-crease origami constructibility? Introduces a `CurvedCrease` structure (γ, θ, κ_g, κ_n) with the Fuchs-Tabachnikov compatibility identity `κ_n = κ_g · cot(θ/2)` encoded as a structure field; proves the straight-fold normal-curvature vanishing lemma; states three sorry-bearing theorems: conservativity over `HHAxioms` (S3 target), algebraic-curve sharpness (S4 target), and the OQ-A open conjecture `K_curved = K_origami` (S5, open mathematics dating to Huffman 1976). S4 (Part 6) adds the explicit `perpBisector` line construction together with the proved reflection law `reflectAcross (perpBisector p₁ p₂ h) p₁ = p₂` and the standalone `hh2_existence` theorem. S5 (Part 7) adds the explicit `perpThroughPoint p ℓ` line construction (fold through `p` perpendicular to `ℓ`) and proves `perpThroughPoint_contains` (the fold passes through `p`) and `reflectAcross_perpThroughPoint_preserves` (reflection across the fold preserves `ℓ` as a set), combining to a standalone `hh4_existence` theorem. S6 (Part 8) adds the explicit `hatoriFold p ℓ₁ ℓ₂ h_nonpar` line construction (fold perpendicular to `ℓ₂` sending `P` onto `ℓ₁`, defined when `crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ≠ 0`), proves `reflectAcross_hatoriFold_preserves_ℓ₂` (fold is perpendicular to ℓ₂) and `reflectAcross_hatoriFold_to_ℓ₁` (reflection of P lands on ℓ₁), combining to a standalone `hh7_existence_nonparallel` theorem — four of the seven HH ingredients (HH-1 via S3, HH-2 via S4, HH-4 via S5, HH-7 non-parallel via S6) required by the eventual full `HHAxioms` witness consumed by `straight_fold_recovers_HH` are now constructive. S7 (Part 9) adds the generic reflection-fixed-point lemma `reflectAcross_self_of_contains` (a point on a line is fixed by reflection across that line) and the standalone `hh7_existence_p_on_ℓ₁` theorem (HH-7 with the side hypothesis `P ∈ ℓ₁`, unconditional in `ℓ₁, ℓ₂` since the perpendicular-from-P fold always works — combining `perpThroughPoint_contains` (S5), the new fixed-point lemma, and `reflectAcross_perpThroughPoint_preserves` (S5)). Together with S6 (`crossDet ≠ 0` case), HH-7 is now constructive on the entire complement of the genuinely-unsolvable parallel-with-P∉ℓ₁ sliver. S8 (Part 10) adds the explicit `parallelBisector ℓ₁ ℓ₂ h_par` line construction for the **parallel case of HH-3** (`crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ = 0`) — the translate-bisector with normal matching `ℓ₁`'s and an algebraic constant term `(s·ℓ₁.c + ℓ₂.c·(ℓ₁.a²+ℓ₁.b²))/(2s)` (where `s = ℓ₁.a·ℓ₂.a + ℓ₁.b·ℓ₂.b`) chosen to land `ℓ₁` onto `ℓ₂` exactly. Proves `parallelBisector_dot_ne_zero` (the denominator `s` is nonzero under parallelism + `ℓ₂.nondeg`), two scaling identities `parallelNormal_left_id` and `parallelNormal_right_id` (`D·ℓ₂.a = s·ℓ₁.a` and `D·ℓ₂.b = s·ℓ₁.b` under `crossDet = 0`), and the main reflection law `reflectAcross_parallelBisector_to_ℓ₂` (every point of `ℓ₁` reflects to a point of `ℓ₂`) via `field_simp + linear_combination` against `hq` and `h_par`. Combines into a standalone `hh3_existence_parallel` theorem — six of the seven HH ingredients (HH-1 via S3, HH-2 via S4, HH-3 parallel via S8, HH-4 via S5, HH-7 via S6+S7) are now constructive; only HH-3 intersecting (requires `Real.sqrt`), HH-5 (Beloch-light) and HH-6 (Beloch fold) remain for subsequent sessions.

originalContributions: CurvedCrease structure: tuple (L, hL, γ, θ, κ_g, κ_n, hθ_pos, ftCompatible) where ftCompatible encodes the Fuchs-Tabachnikov identity κ_n(s) = κ_g(s) · (tan(θ(s)/2))⁻¹ as a structure field
CurvedCrease.IsStraight predicate (geodesic curvature identically zero on [0, L])
normal_curvature_zero_of_straight: proved internal lemma — κ_g ≡ 0 ⇒ κ_n ≡ 0 (algebraic consequence of FT)
CurvedCrease.ExistsHHFold predicate (line through curve endpoints satisfying HHAxioms)
straight_fold_recovers_HH (S3 sorry): conservativity statement — straight curved crease reduces to HH-1
CurveAlgebraic predicate (curve image inside zero-set of bivariate polynomial of degree ≤ d)
curved_fold_algebraic_implies_origami (S4 sorry): algebraic crease curve ⇒ coordinates in K_origami
IsCurvedFoldConstructible predicate (real number is a curved-crease point coordinate)
K_curved_eq_K_origami (S5 sorry, OPEN): formal Lean statement of the Demaine-Demaine-Hart-Price-Tachi 2011 conjecture
perpBisector (S4 def): explicit noncomputable Line construction of the perpendicular bisector of two distinct planar points, in the (a, b, c) ax+by+c=0 normalisation
perpBisector_dirSq_pos (S4 proved): squared chord length is strictly positive when endpoints differ — discharges the reflectAcross denominator
reflectAcross_perpBisector (S4 proved): the perpendicular bisector reflects p₁ onto p₂ — the HH-2 reflection law in explicit form

hh2_existence (S4 proved): standalone HH-2 existence — for any two distinct points, there is a fold line whose reflection sends the first onto the second; matches the HH-2 field of HHAxioms in isolation
perpThroughPoint_normSq_pos (S5 proved): squared norm `ℓ.a² + ℓ.b²` of a line's normal vector is strictly positive — discharges the reflectAcross denominator for HH-4

perpThroughPoint (S5 def): explicit noncomputable Line construction of the fold through `p` perpendicular to `ℓ`, with coefficients `(-ℓ.b, ℓ.a, ℓ.b · p.1 - ℓ.a · p.2)` (normal rotated 90° from `ℓ`, constant chosen to pass through `p`)
perpThroughPoint_contains (S5 proved): the perpendicular fold passes through its anchor point — routine algebra

reflectAcross_perpThroughPoint_preserves (S5 proved): reflection across the perpendicular fold through `p` maps every point of `ℓ` back onto `ℓ` — the HH-4 line-preservation law, via `field_simp` + `linear_combination` exploiting the cancellation `ℓ.a · ℓ.b − ℓ.b · ℓ.a = 0`

hh4_existence (S5 proved): standalone HH-4 existence — for any point `P` and line `ℓ`, there is a fold through `P` whose reflection preserves `ℓ` setwise; matches the HH-4 field of HHAxioms in isolation

crossDet (S6 def): cross-determinant `ℓ₁.b · ℓ₂.a − ℓ₁.a · ℓ₂.b` of two lines' normals; vanishes iff `ℓ₁` and `ℓ₂` are parallel — used as the non-parallel side condition of the Hatori fold construction

hatoriFold (S6 def): explicit noncomputable Line construction of the fold perpendicular to `ℓ₂` that sends `P` onto `ℓ₁`, parametrised by the non-parallel hypothesis `crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ≠ 0`. Coefficients `(-ℓ₂.b, ℓ₂.a, (ℓ₁.a·P.1 + ℓ₁.b·P.2 + ℓ₁.c)·(ℓ₂.a² + ℓ₂.b²)/(2·crossDet) + ℓ₂.b·P.1 − ℓ₂.a·P.2)`

reflectAcross_hatoriFold_preserves_ℓ₂ (S6 proved): reflection across the Hatori fold preserves `ℓ₂` setwise — the perpendicular-to-ℓ₂ property; proof via `simp only` unfolding + `field_simp` + `linear_combination`, mirroring HH-4

reflectAcross_hatoriFold_to_ℓ₁ (S6 proved): reflection of `P` across the Hatori fold lands on `ℓ₁` — the sends-P-to-ℓ₁ property; proof via `simp only` unfolding + `field_simp` + `ring` after `crossDet ≠ 0` is exposed to clear the constant-term denominator

hh7_existence_nonparallel (S6 proved): standalone HH-7 existence (non-parallel case) — for any point `P` and lines `ℓ₁`, `ℓ₂` with `crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ≠ 0`, there is a fold perpendicular to `ℓ₂` sending `P` onto `ℓ₁`; matches the HH-7 field of HHAxioms in isolation modulo the non-parallel restriction (the unconditional parent HHAxioms.hh7 is actually false when ℓ₁∥ℓ₂ ∧ P∉ℓ₁; see the section docstring)

reflectAcross_self_of_contains (S7 proved): a point lying on a line is fixed by reflection across that line — generic primitive shrinking the algebraic boilerplate of any HH-existence proof whose input point already lies on the chosen fold. Proof: the numerator `2 · (l.a · p.1 + l.b · p.2 + l.c)` of the reflection parameter `t` equals zero whenever `p ∈ l`, so `t = 0` and `reflectAcross l p = (p.1, p.2) = p` (via `simp only` with `zero_div`, `zero_mul`, `sub_zero`, `Prod.mk.eta`).

hh7_existence_p_on_ℓ₁ (S7 proved): standalone HH-7 existence in the case `P ∈ ℓ₁` — for any point `P` on `ℓ₁` and any second line `ℓ₂`, the perpendicular fold from `P` through `ℓ₂` (S5's `perpThroughPoint`) preserves `ℓ₂` setwise and fixes `P` (which stays on `ℓ₁`). Unconditional in `ℓ₁, ℓ₂`: the witness works whether or not `ℓ₁ ∥ ℓ₂`. Combined with S6's `hh7_existence_nonparallel`, the only HH-7 case left open is `crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ = 0 ∧ P ∉ ℓ₁`, which per S6 is genuinely unsolvable.

parallelBisector_dot_ne_zero (S8 proved): given two parallel non-degenerate lines (`crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ = 0`), their normal-vector inner product `ℓ₁.a · ℓ₂.a + ℓ₁.b · ℓ₂.b` is nonzero. Proof: assume `s = 0`; combine with `crossDet = 0` via `linear_combination` to derive `(ℓ₁.a² + ℓ₁.b²) · ℓ₂.a = 0` and `(ℓ₁.a² + ℓ₁.b²) · ℓ₂.b = 0`; positivity of `ℓ₁.a² + ℓ₁.b²` forces `ℓ₂.a = 0 ∧ ℓ₂.b = 0`, contradicting `ℓ₂.nondeg`.

parallelBisector (S8 def): explicit noncomputable Line construction of the translate-bisector for two parallel lines. Coefficients `(ℓ₁.a, ℓ₁.b, (s·ℓ₁.c + ℓ₂.c·(ℓ₁.a²+ℓ₁.b²)) / (2s))` where `s = ℓ₁.a·ℓ₂.a + ℓ₁.b·ℓ₂.b`. The normal matches `ℓ₁`'s (so the bisector is parallel to both input lines); the constant term lands every point of `ℓ₁` onto `ℓ₂` under reflection. Non-degeneracy inherited from `ℓ₁.nondeg`.

parallelNormal_left_id, parallelNormal_right_id (S8 proved): under `crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ = 0`, the scaling identities `(ℓ₁.a² + ℓ₁.b²)·ℓ₂.a = s·ℓ₁.a` and `(ℓ₁.a² + ℓ₁.b²)·ℓ₂.b = s·ℓ₁.b` (where `s = ℓ₁.a·ℓ₂.a + ℓ₁.b·ℓ₂.b`). Algebraic content of parallelism: `ℓ₂`'s normal is precisely `(s/D)` times `ℓ₁`'s normal. Each proof is one-line `linear_combination` against the `crossDet = 0` hypothesis.

reflectAcross_parallelBisector_to_ℓ₂ (S8 proved): the HH-3 reflection law in the parallel case — for any point `q ∈ ℓ₁`, the reflection of `q` across `parallelBisector ℓ₁ ℓ₂ h_par` lies on `ℓ₂`. Proof: `simp only` unfolds `Line.contains`, `reflectAcross`, `parallelBisector`; `field_simp` clears the two denominators `(ℓ₁.a² + ℓ₁.b²)` and `2·(ℓ₁.a·ℓ₂.a + ℓ₁.b·ℓ₂.b)`; `linear_combination` closes the residual polynomial identity via `(b·q.1 − a·q.2)·crossDet − s·hq` decomposition.

hh3_existence_parallel (S8 proved): standalone HH-3 existence in the parallel case — for any two parallel non-degenerate lines `ℓ₁`, `ℓ₂` (`crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ = 0`), there exists a fold line whose reflection sends every point of `ℓ₁` to a point of `ℓ₂`. Witness: `parallelBisector ℓ₁ ℓ₂ h_par`. Six of the seven HH ingredients are now constructive (in the parallel-case sense for HH-3 and the `crossDet ≠ 0` ∪ `P ∈ ℓ₁` sense for HH-7); the intersecting case of HH-3 requires `Real.sqrt` for the angle bisector and is deferred.
meta.assumptions: 1 structure-encoded assumption: ftCompatible — the Fuchs-Tabachnikov compatibility identity κ_n(s) = κ_g(s) · cot(θ(s)/2) along the crease. This is the single differential-geometric constraint distinguishing valid smooth curved folds from arbitrary (γ, θ) pairs (Fuchs-Tabachnikov 1999, Theorem 1). Encoded as a field of the `CurvedCrease` structure rather than proved internally because the differential-geometric derivation would require ~350 lines of Darboux-frame curve-on-surface API absent from Mathlib at the pinned revision. Counted as +1 toward axiomCount per the axiom-integrity policy. 0 `axiom` declarations. 3 intentional sorries: S3 straight_fold_recovers_HH conservativity, S4 curved_fold_algebraic_implies_origami partial sharpness, S5 K_curved_eq_K_origami the OQ-A open conjecture (Huffman 1976 / Demaine et al. 2011).

overview.historicalContext: Curved-crease origami was initiated by D. A. Huffman in 1976 (*Curvature and creases: A primer on paper*) and given its modern differential-geometric form by Fuchs and Tabachnikov in 1999 (*More on paperfolding*, Amer. Math. Monthly). The Demaine-Demaine-Hart-Price-Tachi 2011 paper proved that curved-crease origami can trace transcendental crease CURVES (e.g. the elastica family), so the set of curved-fold-constructible curves strictly contains the algebraic curves. Whether the field of curved-fold-constructible POINT COORDINATES strictly contains the origami-constructible field K_origami (characterised by Alperin 2000 / Alperin-Lang 2006 as the field generated by tower extensions of degrees in {2, 3}) is open. The OQ-04 question asks for an axiomatic / algebraic characterisation of K_curved that mirrors the parent file's `origami_degree_classification` (line 575 of `AngleTrisectionOQ05.lean`).
overview.problemStatement: Can the seven straight-crease Huzita-Hatori axioms be strengthened by a finite extension (a single new axiom or a finite schema) to capture exactly the curved-fold-constructible field K_curved? Equivalently, give an axiomatic characterisation of K_curved that mirrors the `α origami-constructible iff [ℚ(α):ℚ] divides 2^a · 3^b` classification. Three candidate strengthenings have been floated informally: (P1) a single curved axiom O8 parametrised by (γ, θ) satisfying the Fuchs-Tabachnikov identity (infinite-dimensional parameter space); (P2) a Beloch-style finite degree-bounded restriction to algebraic γ (finitary but schema-of-axioms); (P3) algebraic-closure-only (loses the geometric primitive). The OQ-04 question asks whether (P1), (P2), (P3) all generate the same field, and whether that field strictly contains K_origami.
overview.text: This file is the S2 ORIENT scaffold for the open question. It introduces a `CurvedCrease` structure carrying (L, γ, θ, κ_g, κ_n) plus the Fuchs-Tabachnikov compatibility identity as a structure field. It proves one internal lemma (straight-fold normal-curvature vanishing) and states three sorry-bearing target theorems: conservativity over HHAxioms (S3), algebraic-curve sharpness (S4), and the OQ-A open conjecture K_curved = K_origami (S5). The status is `axiomatized` because `ftCompatible` is a structure-encoded assumption: the meta `axiomCount` is 1, even though zero `axiom` declarations appear in the file.
overview.proofStrategy: S2 (this file): Encode the differential-geometric content of curved-crease origami as the assumption-bearing structure `CurvedCrease`, where `ftCompatible` is a *field* of the structure rather than a derived theorem. This sidesteps ~350 lines of Darboux-frame curve-on-surface API currently absent from Mathlib at v4.26.0, while keeping the mathematical content faithful: any concrete `CurvedCrease` witness still has to supply a proof that FT holds for its (γ, θ, κ_g, κ_n). The conservativity statement `straight_fold_recovers_HH` is the minimum useful claim: it asserts that the curved-crease formalism is a genuine *extension* of HHAxioms (not a replacement, not weaker). S3 will discharge it via the standard plane-curve characterisation: zero curvature ⇒ line segment ⇒ HH-1.
keyInsights: The Fuchs-Tabachnikov compatibility identity κ_n(s) = κ_g(s) · cot(θ(s)/2) is the SINGLE mathematical constraint distinguishing valid smooth curved folds from arbitrary (γ, θ) pairs (Fuchs-Tabachnikov 1999, Theorem 1).
Straight-fold limit κ_g ≡ 0 forces κ_n ≡ 0 (immediate algebraic consequence of FT) — this is proved internally in this file as `normal_curvature_zero_of_straight`, with no sorry.

Encoding ftCompatible as a structure field rather than proving it internally is an axiom-integrity tradeoff: axiomCount = 1, but the Lean development is tractable today; without this encoding the file would block on ~350 lines of missing Mathlib differential geometry.

Demaine et al. 2011 separate the constructibility of curved CURVES (strictly larger under curved crease) from the constructibility of point COORDINATES (open). OQ-04 is about the latter; the former is settled by the elastica witness.

The conservativity statement `straight_fold_recovers_HH` is the minimum useful S2 deliverable: it asserts that curved-crease origami is a genuine extension of the Huzita-Hatori system, not a replacement.
prerequisites: Algebraic characterization of origami constructibility (`IsOrigamiConstructible`, parent line 182)
Fuchs-Tabachnikov compatibility identity (Theorem 1 of their 1999 paper)

sections.title: The CurvedCrease Structure and IsStraight Predicate
sections.summary: Defines the `CurvedCrease` structure (L, γ, θ, κ_g, κ_n) with `hθ_pos` (fold angle in (0, π) on [0, L]) and `ftCompatible` (Fuchs-Tabachnikov identity κ_n(s) = κ_g(s) · (tan(θ(s)/2))⁻¹). Defines `CurvedCrease.IsStraight` as `∀ s ∈ Set.Icc 0 c.L, c.κg s = 0`.
sections.mathContext: A **curved crease** is a smooth planar curve γ together with a dihedral fold-angle profile θ along it; the geodesic and normal curvatures of γ as a curve on the folded paper surface are linked by the Fuchs-Tabachnikov identity κ_n = κ_g · cot(θ/2). The straight-fold limit κ_g ≡ 0 recovers the classical Huzita-Hatori axioms.

sections.title: Straight-Fold Normal-Curvature Vanishing (proved)
sections.summary: Proves `normal_curvature_zero_of_straight`: if c.IsStraight then c.κn s = 0 for all s ∈ [0, L]. Pure algebraic consequence of ftCompatible: κg s = 0 substituted into κn s = κg s · (tan(θ s / 2))⁻¹ via zero_mul.
sections.mathContext: An immediate corollary of the Fuchs-Tabachnikov identity: with one factor zero, the product is zero, regardless of the dihedral fold-angle profile. No analysis is required.

sections.title: ExistsHHFold Predicate + S3 Conservativity Target
sections.summary: Defines `CurvedCrease.ExistsHHFold` as the existence of an HHAxioms witness together with a Line through both crease endpoints γ 0 and γ L. States `straight_fold_recovers_HH` (S3 sorry): any straight curved crease with distinct endpoints reduces to an HH-1 fold line through those endpoints.
sections.mathContext: Conservativity: the curved-crease formalism is a genuine *extension* of the Huzita-Hatori axiom system. The S3 proof strategy is: (1) κ_n ≡ 0 by `normal_curvature_zero_of_straight`; (2) zero curvature ⇒ γ is a line segment; (3) HH-1 produces the required line through the endpoints.

sections.title: Algebraic-Curve Predicate + S4 Sharpness Target
sections.summary: Defines `CurveAlgebraic γ d` as existence of a non-zero MvPolynomial p in two variables of total degree ≤ d that vanishes on the image of γ. States `curved_fold_algebraic_implies_origami` (S4 sorry): for an algebraic crease curve of degree ≤ d, both coordinates of any γ s lie in the origami-constructible field.
sections.mathContext: Demaine-DHPT 2011, Section 5: rule-line endpoints on an algebraic γ are algebraic over ℚ(γ-coefficients). Combined with Alperin-Lang's degree classification (origami solves all degrees dividing 2^a · 3^b), this gives sharp containment: algebraic curved folds ⊆ K_origami. The S5 conjecture `K_curved = K_origami` would extend this to all (not just algebraic) curved folds.

sections.title: OQ-A Open Conjecture (S5 statement-only)
sections.summary: Defines `IsCurvedFoldConstructible α` as existence of a CurvedCrease c and parameter s ∈ [0, c.L] with α = (c.γ s).1. States `K_curved_eq_K_origami` (S5 PERMANENT sorry, OPEN): for all real α, IsCurvedFoldConstructible α ↔ ∃ d, IsOrigamiConstructible α d.
sections.mathContext: Demaine-DHPT 2011 conjecture: although curved folds can trace transcendental CURVES, the field of constructible POINT COORDINATES is the same as the origami-constructible field. This conjecture is open mathematics dating to Huffman 1976; the Lean statement is intentionally sorry-bearing as a permanent placeholder. The value here is the formal language, not the proof.

sections.title: Summary Comment
sections.summary: Tabular summary of the 8 declarations (1 structure, 4 definitions, 3 statement-only theorems, 1 proved theorem) and the iteration plan S1 (markdown survey) → S2 (this scaffold) → S3 (conservativity proof) → S4 (algebraic sharpness proof) → S5 (OQ-A stays open).
sections.mathContext: S2 ORIENT is the second iteration of a five-session program. The deliverable here is the formal language and three target theorems; S3-S5 will fill in the proofs (S5 intentionally remains open).

sections.title: Constructive HH-2 — Perpendicular Bisector (S4)
sections.summary: Defines `perpBisector p₁ p₂ h : Line` for distinct points with coefficients `(p₂.1 - p₁.1, p₂.2 - p₁.2, -((p₂.1² - p₁.1²) + (p₂.2² - p₁.2²))/2)`. Proves `perpBisector_dirSq_pos` (chord length positive), `reflectAcross_perpBisector` (the HH-2 reflection law `reflectAcross l p₁ = p₂` via `field_simp` + `ring` after Prod.ext split), and `hh2_existence` (standalone HH-2 existence: ∀ p₁ ≠ p₂, ∃ l, reflectAcross l p₁ = p₂). No new sorry is introduced.
sections.mathContext: The perpendicular bisector of two points p₁ ≠ p₂ is the locus of points equidistant from both, equivalently the line through the midpoint perpendicular to the segment p₁p₂. Plugging the (a, b, c) coefficients into the reflection formula `reflectAcross l p = p - 2 (l.a p.1 + l.b p.2 + l.c)/(l.a² + l.b²) · (l.a, l.b)` yields the parameter `t = -1` at p₁, so the reflection adds the direction vector `(p₂.1 - p₁.1, p₂.2 - p₁.2)` to p₁ and lands at p₂. This is the HH-2 axiom of the Huzita-Hatori system in standalone form. Combined with S3's standalone `hh1_existence` (line through two distinct points), two of the seven HH ingredients required by `straight_fold_recovers_HH` are now constructive.

sections.title: Constructive HH-4 — Perpendicular Through a Point (S5)
sections.summary: Defines `perpThroughPoint p ℓ : Line` with coefficients `(-ℓ.b, ℓ.a, ℓ.b · p.1 − ℓ.a · p.2)` (fold's normal is a 90° rotation of `ℓ`'s, constant chosen so the fold passes through `p`). Proves `perpThroughPoint_normSq_pos` (denominator non-vanishing via `ℓ`'s `nondeg` and `sq_pos_of_ne_zero`), `perpThroughPoint_contains` (the fold passes through `p` via `simp` + `ring`), `reflectAcross_perpThroughPoint_preserves` (reflection across the fold preserves `ℓ` setwise, proved by `simp only` unfolding + `field_simp` + `linear_combination`), and `hh4_existence` (standalone HH-4 existence: ∀ p ℓ, ∃ l, l.contains p ∧ ∀ q ∈ ℓ, ℓ.contains (reflectAcross l q)). No new sorry is introduced.
sections.mathContext: The perpendicular fold through `P` orthogonal to a line `ℓ : a x + b y + c = 0` has its own normal vector parallel to `ℓ`'s direction (a 90° rotation of `(ℓ.a, ℓ.b)` gives `(-ℓ.b, ℓ.a)`). Reflection across this fold acts on `ℓ` by reversing direction along `ℓ` while preserving the locus, because the cross-term `ℓ.a · ℓ.b − ℓ.b · ℓ.a` vanishes in the expansion of `ℓ.a · q'.1 + ℓ.b · q'.2 + ℓ.c`. This is the HH-4 axiom of the Huzita-Hatori system in standalone form. Combined with S3's standalone `hh1_existence` (line through two points) and S4's `hh2_existence` (perpendicular bisector), three of the seven HH ingredients required by `straight_fold_recovers_HH` are now constructive; the remaining four are HH-3 (angle bisector), HH-5 (point-on-line via fold through second point), HH-6 (Beloch fold, the cubic-solving one), and HH-7 (Hatori).

sections.title: Constructive HH-7 (non-parallel case) — Hatori Fold (S6)
sections.summary: Defines `crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ := ℓ₁.b·ℓ₂.a − ℓ₁.a·ℓ₂.b` (zero iff lines parallel) and `hatoriFold p ℓ₁ ℓ₂ h_nonpar : Line` with coefficients `(-ℓ₂.b, ℓ₂.a, (ℓ₁.a·p.1 + ℓ₁.b·p.2 + ℓ₁.c)·(ℓ₂.a²+ℓ₂.b²)/(2·crossDet) + ℓ₂.b·p.1 − ℓ₂.a·p.2)`. Proves `hatoriFold_normSq_pos` (denominator non-vanishing, repeats `perpThroughPoint_normSq_pos` specialised to ℓ₂), `reflectAcross_hatoriFold_preserves_ℓ₂` (fold is perpendicular to ℓ₂, mirrors HH-4's proof structure), `reflectAcross_hatoriFold_to_ℓ₁` (reflection of P lands on ℓ₁, via `field_simp` + `ring` after exposing `crossDet ≠ 0`), and `hh7_existence_nonparallel` (standalone HH-7 existence for non-parallel ℓ₁, ℓ₂: ∀ p ℓ₁ ℓ₂, crossDet ≠ 0 → ∃ l, ℓ₁.contains (reflectAcross l p) ∧ ∀ q ∈ ℓ₂, ℓ₂.contains (reflectAcross l q)). No new sorry is introduced.
sections.mathContext: The Hatori axiom HH-7 (Hatori 2001) states that for any point P and lines ℓ₁, ℓ₂, there exists a fold perpendicular to ℓ₂ sending P onto ℓ₁. The unconditional statement is actually false when ℓ₁∥ℓ₂ and P∉ℓ₁: any fold perpendicular to ℓ₂ has direction parallel to ℓ₂'s normal, hence reflects perpendicular to ℓ₂, hence parallel to ℓ₁ (since ℓ₁∥ℓ₂), so perpendicular distance from P to ℓ₁ is invariant. Classical statements of HH-7 therefore tacitly assume ℓ₁ ∦ ℓ₂ (or P∈ℓ₁); this S6 deliverable makes the non-parallel side condition explicit via `crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ≠ 0`. The construction: take fold normal `(-ℓ₂.b, ℓ₂.a)` (90° rotation of ℓ₂'s normal, guaranteeing perpendicularity to ℓ₂) and choose the constant term so the reflection parameter `t = E/crossDet` matches both the perpendicular-to-ℓ₂ requirement and the sends-P-to-ℓ₁ requirement, where `E := ℓ₁.a·P.1 + ℓ₁.b·P.2 + ℓ₁.c` is the signed deviation of P from ℓ₁. After substitution, `ℓ₁.a·P'.1 + ℓ₁.b·P'.2 + ℓ₁.c = E − t·crossDet = E − (E/crossDet)·crossDet = 0`. Combined with S3 (HH-1), S4 (HH-2), and S5 (HH-4), four of the seven HH ingredients required by `straight_fold_recovers_HH` are now constructive; the remaining three are HH-3 (angle bisector), HH-5 (point on line through second point), and HH-6 (Beloch fold, the cubic-solving one).

sections.title: Constructive HH-7 (P-on-ℓ₁ case) — Identity-Like Fold (S7)
sections.summary: Adds `reflectAcross_self_of_contains` (a point on a line is fixed by reflection across that line, via vanishing reflection-parameter numerator) and `hh7_existence_p_on_ℓ₁` (standalone HH-7 existence in the case `P ∈ ℓ₁`, unconditional in `ℓ₁, ℓ₂`: the witness is the perpendicular-from-P fold to ℓ₂ from S5, which preserves ℓ₂ setwise and fixes P). Combined with S6 (`crossDet ≠ 0` case), HH-7 is now constructive on the complement of the genuinely-unsolvable parallel-with-`P∉ℓ₁` sliver. No new sorry or axiom is introduced.
sections.mathContext: When `P ∈ ℓ₁`, any fold through `P` fixes `P` under reflection (the reflection-parameter `t` vanishes since `P` already satisfies the fold's defining equation). The perpendicular fold from `P` to `ℓ₂` — already constructed in S5 as `perpThroughPoint P ℓ₂` — therefore both fixes `P` (keeping it on `ℓ₁`) and preserves `ℓ₂` setwise (its defining property from S5). This witness covers the case `P ∈ ℓ₁` of HH-7 unconditionally in the relative position of `ℓ₁` and `ℓ₂`. Combined with S6's Hatori-fold witness for `crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ ≠ 0`, the constructive coverage of HH-7 is now `{crossDet ≠ 0} ∪ {P ∈ ℓ₁}` — the entire HH-7 statement except the genuinely-unsolvable corner `crossDet = 0 ∧ P ∉ ℓ₁`. The fixed-point lemma `reflectAcross_self_of_contains` is also a reusable primitive: future HH-3/5/6 constructions whose witness fold contains a designated input point can skip the explicit reflection-equation calculation entirely.

sections.title: Constructive HH-3 (parallel case) — Translate Bisector (S8)
sections.summary: Discharges HH-3 in the parallel case (`crossDet ℓ₁ ℓ₂ = 0`) via the translate-bisector. Adds 4 lemmas (`parallelBisector_dot_ne_zero`, `parallelNormal_left_id`, `parallelNormal_right_id`, `reflectAcross_parallelBisector_to_ℓ₂`) + 1 definition (`parallelBisector`) + the standalone existence theorem `hh3_existence_parallel`. Six of seven HH ingredients now constructive; only HH-3 intersecting (`Real.sqrt`-bound), HH-5 (Beloch-light), and HH-6 (Beloch fold) remain.
sections.mathContext: When two lines are parallel, the unique reflection mapping one onto the other (setwise) is across the line midway between them — the *translate-bisector*. Unlike the intersecting case (which requires angle bisectors and `Real.sqrt`), the translate-bisector admits an explicit `noncomputable def` over `ℝ` with no transcendental ingredients: its normal vector is identical to `ℓ₁`'s and its constant term is a rational function of the input coefficients. The geometric content of parallelism — that normals are proportional — surfaces algebraically as the two scaling identities `D·ℓ₂.a = s·ℓ₁.a` and `D·ℓ₂.b = s·ℓ₁.b`, both consequences of `crossDet = 0`.

conclusion.summary: S2 ORIENT scaffold: a CurvedCrease structure with the Fuchs-Tabachnikov identity κ_n = κ_g · cot(θ/2) as a structure field, one proved internal lemma (straight-fold ⇒ κ_n ≡ 0), and three sorry-bearing target theorems for S3-S5 iterations. The status is `axiomatized` (badge `axiom`) because `ftCompatible` is a structure-encoded assumption — axiomCount = 1, sorries = 3, axiom-declarations = 0.
conclusion.implications: The formal language fixed in this file (CurvedCrease, IsStraight, ExistsHHFold, CurveAlgebraic, IsCurvedFoldConstructible) is the natural starting point for any axiomatic treatment of curved-crease origami. The conservativity statement straight_fold_recovers_HH (S3 target) is the minimum useful claim: it asserts that any candidate strengthening of HHAxioms must reduce to HHAxioms in the straight-fold limit, ruling out replacement-style extensions. The algebraic-sharpness statement curved_fold_algebraic_implies_origami (S4 target) is the natural Lean analogue of the Demaine et al. 2011 algebraic-curve result. The OQ-A statement K_curved_eq_K_origami (S5) is a permanent open-mathematics placeholder — its value is the formal language, not the proof.
openQuestions: OQ-A (K_curved = K_origami): Does the curved-fold-constructible field strictly contain the origami-constructible field? Demaine-DHPT 2011 conjecture FALSE (no strict containment); proof open since Huffman 1976.
OQ-B (K_curved ⊆ K_(ω-fold)): Is the curved-fold-constructible field contained in the ω-fold straight-origami field (= all algebraic numbers)? Folklore YES; no formal proof.

OQ-C (the OQ-04 question itself): Does any of the three candidate axiom schemata — (P1) single curved axiom O8 parametrised by (γ, θ); (P2) Beloch-style finite degree-bounded restriction; (P3) algebraic-closure-only — generate K_curved? Open whether (P1), (P2), (P3) all give the same field.
